mem.7:
May 8, 2023 — Caroline and Melanie (“Mel”) caught up. Mel was busy with work and children. Caroline had attended an LGBTQ support group the day before; hearing trans people’s stories made her feel accepted, supported, and more courageous about embracing herself. She planned to continue her education and explore counseling/mental-health careers to help people with similar experiences. Mel said she’d make a good counselor. Caroline shared a photo of a dog walking past a wall painted with a woman; Mel liked the painting. Mel shared her 2022 painting of a sunrise over a lake, which she valued for self-expression, creativity, and relaxation. Caroline praised the colors. Caroline left to research; Mel went swimming with her kids.

May 25, 2023 — Mel said she had run a mental-health charity race on May 20. It made her reflect on well-being and self-care; she was trying to make daily time for running, reading, or violin, though self-care remained a work in progress. Her kids were excited for summer; family was considering camping in June. Caroline was researching adoption agencies. Having a family and giving children in need a loving home had long been her dream. She shared a photo of an adoption-agency sign/building. She chose the agency because it supports LGBTQ+ adopters and felt hopeful, though she had much to learn. She looked forward to creating a family, while aware single parenting would be challenging. Mel said she’d be an awesome mom; Caroline hoped to offer a safe, loving home, and Mel felt she would provide love and stability.

June 9, 2023 — Caroline described speaking at a school event the previous week about her transgender journey and encouraging student involvement in the LGBTQ community. She felt powerful sharing struggles, coming out, and personal growth; audience members related and were inspired to be better allies. She said conversations about gender identity and inclusion promote understanding, acceptance, and hope. Caroline began transitioning around 2020. Mel praised her courage and advocacy. Caroline called friends, family, and mentors her “rocks”; she had known her support-network friends for four years, since moving from her home country around 2019. Their support was especially important after a difficult breakup. Caroline shared a family/friends photo in a yard. Mel said her husband and children motivate and support her; she and her husband had been married five years (since around 2018). She shared a photo of a man and little girl in front of a waterfall and a wedding photo of herself in a dress holding a bouquet. Caroline congratulated her. Mel also shared a family picnic photo (man and woman sitting on a blanket eating); she treasured the games, food, and time together, which made her feel alive and happy. Caroline agreed that time with loved ones brings gratitude and happiness; family is everything.

June 27, 2023 — Caroline shared a photo of a necklace with a cross and heart, a childhood gift from her grandmother in Sweden. It represents love, faith, and strength, and reminds her of her roots and family’s support. Mel shared patterned bowls and asked about treasured objects. Caroline’s friend had made her a hand-painted bowl for her 18th birthday, ten years earlier (around 2013); its design and colors remind her of art and self-expression. Mel said she had taken her family camping in the mountains the previous week (around June 20): nature walks, hiking, campfire marshmallows, and an amazing summit view. Her two younger children love nature; she treasured the trip. Caroline was glad they made memories.

Caroline remained interested in counseling/mental-health work, possibly supporting trans people’s self-acceptance and mental health. She shared a bookshelf photo and described attending an LGBTQ+ counseling workshop on Friday, June 23, about therapeutic approaches and working effectively with trans people. It was enlightening; professionals’ dedication to safe spaces inspired her. Counseling and support groups had helped her own journey and motivated her to create a welcoming place for others. Mel encouraged her and also shared a photo of a bookshelf in a room.

July 3, 2023 — Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ+ pride parade the previous week. Its joyful atmosphere made her feel she belonged and showed how much the community had grown. It motivated her to use her story to help others; she remained excited about counseling/mental-health work. Mel had signed up for a pottery class the day before; she found pottery therapeutic, creative, and expressive. She shared a photo of someone holding a frisbee and one of a bowl she made, decorated with a black-and-white flower. She was proud of it and said pottery was important in her life, helping her express emotions and bringing joy. Caroline praised her creativity and said she was learning piano. Caroline planned to attend a transgender conference in July to meet people and learn about advocacy; Mel wished her fun and safety.

July 6, 2023 — Caroline had been looking further into counseling/mental-health work; helping people and making a positive impact felt challenging but rewarding. Mel said she took her kids to a museum on July 5 and shared a photo of two children playing in a water-play area. They especially enjoyed the dinosaur exhibit, learning about animals, and seeing bones; it reminded Mel why she loves being a mom. Caroline said motherhood was awesome and she was building a library for her future children, with children’s classics, stories from different cultures, and educational books. She shared a bookcase photo and looked forward to reading with them. Mel’s favorite childhood book was *Charlotte’s Web*; friendship and compassion meant a lot to her. She shared a photo of a cover showing a girl and cat. Caroline said those themes made her appreciate friends and family who helped her through transition. Caroline had picnicked with friends the previous week and shared a photo of women sitting on a blanket in a park. Her support network gave love, guidance, and acceptance throughout her transition; their unconditional encouragement helped her accept and grow into her true self, and she couldn’t have done it without them. Mel also shared a photo of her family camping at a beach campfire; they love it and feel closer together.

July 12, 2023 — Caroline said she had attended an LGBTQ conference on July 10. Meeting people with similar journeys in a welcoming environment made her feel accepted and grateful for the community. It reinforced the importance of fighting for trans rights and spreading awareness. She noted progress but said more was needed and wanted to help. She was still looking into counseling and mental-health jobs so people would have someone to talk to. Her own mental-health struggles and helpful support had motivated her to help others on similar journeys. Mel praised her and shared a photo of a book cover with a gold coin; a book she read the previous year reminded her to pursue dreams. Caroline said books guide and motivate her and help her discover herself. Her favorite was *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt, a true story about a trans girl and her family; it made Caroline feel connected and hopeful. She shared a photo of a dog in a boat on the water. The book taught her self-acceptance, finding support, and that hard times don’t last; hope and love exist. They agreed pets bring joy and comfort. Mel shared photos of two little girls on steps with a dog and a cat lying on the floor. Her family has a dog and cat named Luna and Oliver; they are sweet, playful, and brighten the house. Mel also shared pink sneakers (Caroline called the color purple); they were running shoes. Mel had been running farther since the prior chat to destress and clear her mind, improving her mental health, and planned to continue. She had shared photos of the shoes being worn and in a box. Caroline encouraged her and emphasized self-care and mental health.
mem.13:

**8 May 2023** — Caroline said an LGBTQ support group helped her feel accepted and braver about embracing herself. She planned further education and to explore counseling or mental-health work. They shared art photos: Caroline’s dog by a mural and Mel’s 2022 sunrise-over-lake painting. Mel was busy with work and kids; Caroline went to research, and Mel swam with her children.

**25 May 2023** — Mel had run a mental-health charity race on 20 May and was trying to make time for running, reading, or violin. Her family considered camping in June. Caroline researched adoption agencies, a long-held dream of giving a child a loving home; she chose one supportive of LGBTQ adopters. She knew single parenting could be hard but wanted to provide safety and love. Mel said she would be a wonderful mother.

**9 June 2023** — Caroline spoke at a school event about being trans and LGBTQ involvement. She began transitioning around 2020; sharing her story helped others understand and become better allies. Friends, family, and mentors supported her, especially after a difficult breakup. She moved from her home country around 2019 and had known some supportive friends for four years. Mel said her husband and kids motivate her; she and her husband had been married five years (since about 2018). She shared family, wedding, and picnic photos; games, food, and time together make her happy.

**27 June 2023** — Caroline’s cross-and-heart necklace was a childhood gift from her grandmother in Sweden; it represents love, faith, strength, roots, and family support. A friend hand-painted her a bowl for her 18th birthday (about 2013), reminding her of art and self-expression. Mel’s family camped in the mountains around 20 June, hiking, having campfires and marshmallows, and enjoying a summit view. Caroline attended an LGBTQ counseling workshop on 23 June and wants to create welcoming spaces. They shared bookshelf photos.

**3–6 July 2023** — Caroline attended a pride parade and planned a transgender conference; pride reinforced her sense of belonging and advocacy/counseling ambitions. Mel began pottery, finding it therapeutic; she shared a handmade flower bowl and frisbee. Caroline was learning piano. Mel took her kids to a museum on 5 July; they loved the dinosaur exhibits. Caroline was building a future children’s library, including multicultural and educational books. Mel’s childhood favorite was *Charlotte’s Web*; its themes reminded Caroline of supportive friends. Caroline had picnicked with friends; Mel shared a family beach-campfire photo.

**12 July 2023** — Caroline attended an LGBTQ conference on 10 July, renewing her commitment to trans rights and awareness, and continued looking into counseling work. Her favorite book is *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt; it brought hope, connection, self-acceptance, and appreciation of support. Mel’s pets are Luna (dog) and Oliver (cat); both said pets bring comfort. Mel runs farther to destress and support mental health; she shared pink shoes, which Caroline thought were purple.

**15–17 July 2023** — Mel took her kids to pottery on 14 July; they made pots and sculptures. Her family painted a sunset/palm-tree scene and found purple flowers. Caroline attended an adoption council meeting on 14 July, strengthening her resolve. Mel shared a vase of sunflowers and roses; Caroline’s favorite color is blue, and she associates sunflowers with warmth/happiness and roses with love/beauty. Flowers featured in Mel’s wedding; her favorite moment was marrying her partner. Caroline described pride as joyful, safe, and freeing; being herself without fear and having community support helped her mental health. Mel finds peace in creativity and family; camping and mountain hikes are family favorites. Caroline joined an LGBTQ youth mentorship program the prior weekend and mentors a trans teen; she treasures seeing the mentee feel supported. She planned an LGBTQ art show in August. They shared paintings: Caroline’s tree/sun artwork followed a visit to an LGBTQ center and represents unity/strength; Mel and her kids painted together.

**20 July 2023** — Caroline joined “Connected LGBTQ Activists,” who meet regularly to plan campaigns and support one another. Mel shared beach and camping memories with her three children: kite play, sandcastles, campfire stories, and seeing the Perseid meteor shower the previous year. She felt tiny and awed under the stars. Her youngest’s first steps are a cherished reminder that life moves quickly.

**14 August 2023** — Mel said she celebrated her daughter’s birthday the previous night, 13 August, at a Matt Patterson concert; she loved seeing her kids happy. Caroline shared that she attended a pride parade on 11 August, feeling proud and energized to advocate for equality. Photos included a welcoming band and a crowd with balloons; Mel had concert photos. Caroline said she represents inclusion and diversity in her art and uses it to advocate for LGBTQ acceptance. Her art expresses her trans experience and helps others understand trans people. Her painting “Embracing Identity” depicts a woman and is about finding comfort, love, and self-acceptance. Art helps Caroline explore transition and her changing body, process experiences, and accept the beauty of imperfections. Mel praised it as healing and affirming.

**17 August 2023** — Caroline recounted a distressing hike encounter with religious conservatives who said something upsetting; it reminded her how much work remains for LGBTQ rights. She feels she will be okay because she has accepting, supportive people around her. Mel shared a photo of a colorful patterned bowl from her latest pottery project. She loves bright colors and patterns and made it to catch the eye and make people smile; painting lets her express feelings, with each stroke carrying part of her. She described art as a learning experience, sanctuary, comfort, and source of happiness and fulfillment. They affirmed that finding joyful moments helps them through life’s struggles and expressed gratitude for their friendship and support. Caroline shared a photo of a group walking down a street with balloons, recalling their fun together at the Pride festival the previous year. They agreed to plan something special for the summer; Caroline suggested a family outing or an outing for just the two of them to catch up and explore nature. Mel would think of ideas; both looked forward to making memories.

**23 August 2023** — Caroline applied to adoption agencies, calling it her first step toward becoming a mom. An adoption advice/assistance group had helped her. She felt excited but nervous about parenting’s responsibility; Mel congratulated her and wished her well. Caroline has a guinea pig named Oscar, who likes vegetables, especially parsley; she shared a photo of him eating parsley. Mel said her pets were doing well and that they had added a cat named Bailey. They discussed pets and shared photos: Mel’s photo described as Oliver was of a black dog lying in grass with a frisbee; Caroline shared Oscar in a cage with hay. Mel recalled Oliver hiding his bone in her slipper, and told of feeding a horse a carrot. Caroline loved horses and remembered riding through fields with her father as a child. Mel shared a horse painting she had made on a wooden wall; she loves painting animals because it is peaceful and special, and admires horses’ grace. Caroline shared a recent self-portrait of a woman with a blue face, painted the previous week. She felt liberated and empowered while making it; art helps her explore identity, be true to herself, and is therapeutic. She said freedom also comes from supportive people, promoting LGBTQ rights, and living authentically; she wants to help others do the same. Mel praised her and offered support.

Favorite book: *Becoming Nicole* by Amy Ellis Nutt; it gave hope, connection, and self-acceptance. She was learning piano and building a future children’s library. Mel began pottery as therapy, took the kids to a dinosaur museum on 5 July, and shared a family beach-campfire photo. Mel’s childhood favorite was *Charlotte’s Web*. Pets: Luna (dog), Oliver (cat), later Bailey (cat). Mel runs to destress; Caroline thought Mel’s pink shoes were purple.

Caroline’s favorite color is blue; sunflowers suggest warmth/happiness, roses love/beauty. Pride feels joyful, safe, freeing, and good for her mental health. Caroline joined LGBTQ youth mentorship and treasures seeing her trans teen mentee supported. She planned an August LGBTQ art show; a tree/sun artwork represented unity and strength. On 20 July she joined “Connected LGBTQ Activists,” which met regularly for campaigns/support. Mel shared beach camping with her three children, kites, sandcastles, campfire stories, the prior year’s Perseid meteor shower, and cherishes her youngest’s first steps.

**14–28 August** — Mel celebrated her daughter’s birthday on 13 August at a Matt Patterson concert. Caroline attended a Pride parade on 11 August and felt proud/energized to advocate equality. Her art explores inclusion, identity, and transition: “Embracing Identity” depicts a woman and represents comfort, love, self-acceptance, and accepting imperfections; a blue-faced self-portrait felt liberating. Mel finds painting and pottery a sanctuary for feelings, comfort, learning, and joy. Caroline had distressing hiking encounters with religious conservatives; one later went badly and she tried to apologize. Supportive acceptance from the trans community made a huge difference. Her rainbow-flag mural represented trans courage/strength; an eagle, freedom/pride/resilience. She volunteered at an LGBTQ+ youth center, gratifyingly helping young people feel less alone; they were organizing a talent show for the following month. Mel volunteered at a homeless shelter and found witnessing neglect difficult. Caroline plays guitar (began acoustic around 2018); “Brave” by Sara Bareilles is meaningful. Mel has played clarinet since childhood; likes Bach, Mozart, and Ed Sheeran’s “Perfect.” Caroline’s guinea pig Oscar likes vegetables, especially parsley. Mel said Oliver hid a bone in her slipper and she fed a horse a carrot; Caroline rode horses with her father as a child and loves them.

**13 September** — Caroline enjoyed a refreshing bike outing with friends the previous weekend; shared beach/fence/sunset photo. Mel shared yellow-leaved forest road; her family had camped and hiked, roasting marshmallows and telling stories. Caroline said volunteering, supportive friends/family/mentors, and art help her make a difference and express what words can’t. She has made art since about age 17; painting helped explore gender identity. A red-and-blue painting represented the binary gender system; mixing colors challenged rigid thinking. Transition changed relationships: some friends stayed supportive, others couldn’t handle it; Caroline is happier and relationships now feel more genuine. Mel shared a café-door sign that worried Caroline; Mel clarified it was only a precaution and she had a great time.

**13 October** — Caroline contacted her mentor for adoption advice, saying she felt ready to be a mother and offer a safe, loving home. Mel’s friend adopted the previous year after a long process and was happy; Mel wondered about adopting. Caroline advised researching agencies/lawyers, gathering references and financial/medical documents, and preparing emotionally for the wait. Mel had been injured the previous month and paused pottery; she was okay, reading a book Caroline recommended and painting. Mel shared calming pink-sky sunset painting, then abstract blue-background painting; blue streaks showed tranquility amid vibrant colors. Caroline had recently tried abstract art for spontaneous emotional expression. She attended a transgender poetry reading the previous Friday, a safe, empowering space; shared classroom poster and “Trans Lives Matter” sign photos. Inspired, she drew a woman in a dress symbolizing freedom, authenticity, and embracing womanhood. They affirmed being oneself is an ongoing journey.

**20 October** — Mel recounted a frightening family road trip the previous weekend: her son was in an accident but was okay; shared dashboard/steering-wheel photo. It reminded her life is precious and family matters. Her children were scared, but she reassured them; she said they are resilient and give her strength, and family is her biggest motivation/support. They enjoyed visiting the Grand Canyon; shared photo of two children on rocky overlook. On 19 October they took a relaxing trail walk (photo of woman and child walking). Nature helps Mel reset; she loves camping for peaceful family time, stories, campfires, birdsong, and fresh air. Shared sunset over water.

**22 October 2023** — Caroline passed adoption agency interviews the previous Friday and was excited; a major step toward having a family. Mel congratulated her and shared a photo of two wooden dolls on a table, saying they reminded her of family love; asked Caroline’s future vision. Caroline wants to build her own family and give children without a home a safe, loving roof; adoption is giving back and showing love/acceptance. She believes everyone deserves acceptance and wants children to experience it. Her long path to self-acceptance, transition, and support from friends, family, and role models inspired her to support others; helping them find comfort and grow brings joy. Mel called her strong and inspiring. Caroline shared a green/yellow-designed clock photo and a painting with “happiness” written on it; she said living honestly and being oneself feels freeing. They value being there for each other.
